How about taking it even further?

We could have a feature to post to multiple subverses and be able to add subverses to it later when suggested that "/v/randomsub would love this!". In this case, subverses would act as a sort of tags. Then when a post gets removed from a sub, it just means that it lost the "tag" and the post's author can add a different tag to it to make it show up in a different sub.

It could be that a post, if not deleted, can have no less than one tag. Mods could then tag posts with a different subverse and remove the original tag to "move" it over.

To prevent removing and re-adding tags ad nauseam, it could be that tags can only be added or removed for a week or so after a post has been posted and only once a day per tag (and a tag could be locked out by mods so that the user can't re-add the unwanted tag).

There'd be a lot to think about regarding this matter, but I don't think it's a bad idea at its core.

I actually think the site would be better without this feature. If people want to post to multiple subverses, then they should do so individually. Otherwise people are likely to try spamming every subverse that seems half-relevant.

This empowers mods for very little gain. If we're to avoid the issues Reddit ran into it's important that mods remain as impotent as possible. If what was posted was against the rules of a sub then the post can be deleted and the user given a message suggesting a more appropriate forum. A moderate being able to opaquely and unilaterally do this all himself is not desirable.

In any case it obviously should be up to the user in what context they want their submission discussed. The general tone and level of discussion is going to vary radically between politics and conspiracy, for instance.
